text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Stonehaven private VPC: intermittent egress probe oscillation and customer-facing timeouts (NLB health checks failing). Pager: @maria_sre.

maria_sre: Acknowledged. Paging on-call and standing up in #incidents.

stonehaven_ops: We're seeing ~30% checkout requests to external payment provider time out (504) starting 2026-03-17T10:23Z. Impacting EU customers.

tom_infra: Looking at NLB -> target logs now. Health checks are intermittently timing out. Targets respond but conntrack on instances is very high.

rachel_eng: Quick question — any recent SG or route changes in the last 2 hours? I don't see infra deploys in the runbook window.

ops_lead: No deploys from Redwood infra. Customer said they rotated some IP allow lists this morning — @stonehaven_ops can you confirm?

stonehaven_ops: We rotated outbound allowlist for a few 3rd-party endpoints (payment vendor) at 09:50Z, but that was limited to a subnet-level rule. Shouldn't affect internal target groups.

maria_sre: Pulled conntrack and system stats from node stone-vpc-1b-03.

maria_sre (logs): ```
# conntrack -S
entries: 923456
tcp: 812345
udp: 111111
# /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max = 1000000
# iptables -L -n shows no unexpected DNAT
```

tom_infra: NAT gateway metrics show ephemeral port exhaustion on the tenant NAT instance (high ephemeral port reuse). NLB health checks originate from the LB and hit instance ports; with ephemeral exhaustion probes may not complete.

ops_lead: Two parallel mitigations: 1) Reduce target group weight for impacted ASG members and drain 2 nodes and clear conntrack; 2) Canary shift a percentage of traffic to Redwood Dedicated fallback pool (redwood-dedicated-eu-1). Agree?

rachel_eng: +1. Also validate SG egress rules allow health check responses back to the NLB source range. Runbook step: verify `aws ec2 describe-security-groups` for tenant SG.

tom_infra: Executing step 1. Deregistering targets (2 nodes) from TG, then SSH and flush conntrack. Commands:```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu:... --targets Id=i-0abc123
ssh ec2-user@stone-vpc-1b-03 'sudo conntrack -F && sudo systemctl restart networking'
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu:... --targets Id=i-0abc123
```

alan_support: Notifying account team and Stonehaven on status. Sending holding message: "We're investigating traffic issues; short mitigation in progress."

stonehaven_ops: Thanks. Please confirm expected impact of draining nodes (small, rolling) vs full outage.

maria_sre: Rolling drain is safe; we'll do one node at a time and monitor error rate. Starting node 03 drain now (10:35Z).

incident-bot: Update: incident assigned to maria_sre and tom_infra. Priority: P1.

(10:38Z) tom_infra: Cleared conntrack on node 03 and re-registered. Observed immediate drop in ephemeral collisions.

(10:42Z) rachel_eng: Quick SG check: tenant-sg-eu allows outbound 0.0.0.0/0 on ephemeral ports, inbound from NLB range OK. No recent SG denies.

ops_lead: Initiating canary traffic shift 30% -> redwood-dedicated-eu-1 using traffic control policy. Command: `console: route-shift --target redwood-dedicated-eu-1 --weight 30 --note "Stonehaven egress canary"`

alan_support: Account notified: "We have initiated mitigations (node drain + canary shift). Monitoring metrics and will update in 10 min."

(10:50Z) stonehaven_ops: Error rate on checkout pages dropping from 30% -> 7%. Still seeing intermittent timeouts but much improved.

maria_sre: Cleared conntrack on node 04 as well. Drains done on 2/6 nodes. Overall conntrack usage now ~54%.

tom_infra: NAT ephemeral port reuse metric decreased; NLB health checks passing across target group now.

ops_lead: Current customer impact: reduced but not fully resolved. Proposed next steps: continue roll drains until conntrack < 60% across nodes, keep canary shift at 30% until stable, start capacity increase for NAT instance if ephemeral usage trends back up.

stonehaven_ops: Account team requests an ETA — can we provide one? Customers still report a small fraction of failed payments.

maria_sre: ETA for core mitigations (conntrack drain + canary) is ~20 minutes. We'll reassess and either rollback shift or move to full 100% to dedicated if health deteriorates.

(11:05Z) alan_support: Update to customer: "Mitigations applied; we are monitoring. Expecting stable behavior within 15-25 minutes."

(11:07Z) incident-bot: Timeline note added.

(11:10Z) tom_infra: Conntrack steady, health checks green, error rate down to 2.1% for last 5m. Keeping incident open for post-mortem and long-term fix (increase conntrack table, tune NAT, consider ephemeral port allocation changes).

maria_sre: Assigning follow-ups: (1) run long-term tuning runbook with customer (ops_lead + rachel_eng), (2) prepare postmortem draft with timelines and root cause hypotheses (maria_sre).

ops_lead: Thanks team. I'll update status to SE and account. Closing active mitigation steps; monitoring for 1 hour then reduce canary shift.

stonehaven_ops: Appreciate the rapid response. We'll hold on any further config changes at our end until postmortem.

maria_sre: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Leaving thread open for final confirmation and postmortem notes.
